story.head: The matchup inside the matchup
paras: The Blues (6-6-1) beat Boston 4-1 on Oct 29, and the Devils (9-5-0) beat Vegas 5-2 on Friday. Going in, the Blues are fifth in the Central (tied for 22nd in the NHL) and the Devils second in the Metropolitan (tied for sixth).

The Blues have played better than their record (.500) says: their chances are worth about .588, and their finishing has held them back. So have the Devils (.643 on chances worth .741), where their goaltending has held them back.

The Blues (lowest) and the Devils (2nd lowest) both keep things calm after the whistle. The Blues keep dangerous shots away better than almost anyone (2nd), but have struggled on the power play (31st). On the other side, the Devils throw more pucks at the net than almost anyone (3rd) and get pinned in their own end on long shifts (30th). The Devils’ power play against the Blues’ penalty killers is strength against strength. On top of that, the Blues’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Devils’ not so much.

Dylan Holloway (3 G / 8 A / 11 P in 13 GP) leads the Blues in scoring, and Jimmy Snuggerud (7 G / 2 A / 9 P in 13 GP) has a team-high seven goals. For the Devils, Jack Hughes (6 G / 10 A / 16 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Arseny Gritsyuk (8 G / 4 A / 12 P in 14 GP) has a team-high eight goals.
Joel Hofer (5-3-1 / .923 SV% in 9 GS) has been outstanding for St. Louis and will likely start. Jake Allen (5-3-0 / .886 SV% in 8 GS) is in line to start for New Jersey.
